documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Seen 01/22/2024

Ulcerative colitis, one year from diagnosis. She remains well on mesalamine 800 mg three times daily: formed stools once or twice daily, no bleeding, no nocturnal symptoms. She asked whether the doses could be combined; since she is doing well on the current regimen I would rather not change it this year, and she agreed.

Interval history notable for recurrence of her breast cancer in bone, on letrozole and zoledronic acid through oncology. Creatinine stable on her quarterly labs.

Exam: abdomen soft, nontender.

Plan: continue mesalamine 800 mg TID. Follow-up in one year, sooner for any return of bleeding.

documents.title: Rheumatology visit - right hip pain
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Re: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Visit 03/27/2024

Ms. Jacobs came in for her scheduled RA visit with three months of progressively worsening right hip pain. It is deep and aching, worse with weight bearing, and does not ease with rest. No injury. No fever, chills, weight loss or night sweats. Her hands and wrists have been quiet.

Background: long-standing RA on methotrexate, folic acid and daily prednisone; osteoporosis; ulcerative colitis; metastatic breast cancer in bone, on letrozole and zoledronic acid; hypertension on amlodipine and HCTZ; hyperlipidemia.

Exam: right hip with limited internal rotation and abduction and mild groin tenderness. No overlying redness, swelling or warmth. Neurovascular exam of both legs normal. No small-joint synovitis.

Assessment: right hip pain with restricted rotation in a patient on chronic glucocorticoids and with known bone metastases. Avascular necrosis is the main concern; a metastatic lesion must be excluded.

Plan: MRI of the pelvis without contrast (ordered, scheduled 3/29). Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid and prednisone 5 mg. I will call her with the result.

Addendum 04/01/2024: MRI shows avascular necrosis of the right femoral head without collapse; no metastatic lesion in the pelvis or proximal femurs. Discussed with patient; recommend orthopedic evaluation.

Rheumatology

conditions.label: Avascular necrosis of femoral head, right

reports.text: MRI of the pelvis and both hips without contrast. Indication: right hip pain, history of breast cancer metastatic to bone, chronic steroids. Right femoral head: serpiginous subchondral low-signal line in the anterosuperior femoral head with surrounding bone marrow edema. Articular surface preserved, no subchondral collapse or fracture. Left femoral head normal. No focal marrow-replacing lesion in the pelvis or proximal femora. Sacroiliac joints unremarkable. Visualized pelvic soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Avascular necrosis of the right femoral head without collapse. No osseous metastatic lesion in the pelvis or proximal femora.

documents.title: Hip MRI
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Rheumatology called me about the MRI. She said the hip bone isn't getting enough blood and I should see an orthopedic doctor. Can you send the referral? And it is NOT the cancer, which I was very relieved to hear.

documents.title: RE: Hip MRI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes - that's avascular necrosis of the right femoral head, and the MRI shows the bone has kept its shape, which is good news. I've placed the orthopedic referral today. Until you see them, use the acetaminophen as needed and go easy on long walks; a cane in your left hand will take some load off the right hip.

documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
ORTHOPAEDIC SURGERY CONSULTATION
Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Date of service 04/22/2024

Referred for right femoral head avascular necrosis seen on MRI 3/29/2024. Four months of right groin pain with weight bearing. Risk factors include long-term prednisone. Also has bone-only metastatic breast cancer on letrozole and zoledronic acid, RA on methotrexate, ulcerative colitis.

Exam: right hip internal rotation and abduction limited and painful at end range. No leg length discrepancy. Distal neurovascular exam intact.

Imaging: MRI reviewed - pre-collapse lesion in the anterosuperior head, no collapse.

Assessment: right femoral head AVN, pre-collapse.

Plan: nonoperative management for now.
- Protected weight bearing with a cane in the left hand.
- Physical therapy for hip range of motion and gait.
- Acetaminophen as needed; avoid NSAIDs given her colitis and medications.
- Radiographs in 6 months to look for collapse.
Return in 6 months.

Orthopaedic Surgery

reports.text: Whole-body planar imaging after IV Tc-99m MDP, compared with 11/08/2023. Previously noted uptake at T7, T10 and the right 6th and 8th ribs is unchanged in distribution and intensity. No new foci.
reports.conclusion: Stable osseous metastatic disease. No new lesions.

documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY
Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Visit 04/29/2024

Bone-only metastatic breast cancer, on letrozole 2.5 mg daily and zoledronic acid every 4 weeks since 12/2023, tolerating both. Restaging bone scan 4/24: stable, no new lesions. CA 27-29 today 34 U/mL (64 before treatment; reference <38). Interval MRI for hip pain showed right femoral head AVN, not metastasis; orthopedics is managing nonoperatively.

Exam: spine nontender; uses a cane.

Plan: continue letrozole. Continue zoledronic acid 4 mg every 4 weeks with creatinine before each dose. Bone scan again in 6 months. Reminded her to tell her dentist about the zoledronic acid.

orders.reason: exposed bone at extraction site, on zoledronic acid

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: jaw pain after tooth extraction

HPI: Lower posterior molar extracted 8/26 by her dentist. Pain and swelling of the lower jaw began shortly afterward and have not settled. Feels a rough edge with her tongue. No fever, eating soft foods. On zoledronic acid q4wk since 12/2023 for bone mets (last dose 9/9), alendronate 2021-2023 before that. Also chronic prednisone and MTX.

Exam: afebrile per vitals. Mild swelling along the lower jaw. Intraoral: at the extraction socket, an area of exposed yellow-white bone, no pus. No neck nodes.

A/P: Exposed bone at a recent extraction site in a patient on monthly zoledronic acid - concerning for medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw.
- Urgent ENT referral (head and neck), appointment 9/23.
- Message sent to oncology re: zoledronic acid; they will hold further doses pending ENT.
- Soft diet, careful brushing, acetaminophen for pain.
- Call for fever, pus or spreading swelling.

documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OTOLARYNGOLOGY - HEAD AND NECK SURGERY
Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Date of service 09/23/2024

Reason for referral: lower jaw pain and swelling after dental extraction.

HPI: Three weeks of pain and swelling of the lower jaw that started soon after a tooth extraction on 8/26. She receives zoledronic acid every 4 weeks for osteoporosis and bone metastases from breast cancer (since 12/2023; alendronate before that).

PMH: metastatic breast cancer to bone on letrozole, osteoporosis, RA on methotrexate and prednisone, ulcerative colitis on mesalamine, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, right femoral head AVN. NKDA. Former smoker.

Vitals: T 37.2 C, BP 130/85, pulse 78.

Exam: swelling over the mandible. Intraoral exam shows exposed necrotic bone at the extraction site. No purulence. No cervical or submandibular lymphadenopathy. Remainder of head and neck exam normal.

Labs today: WBC 7.5, hemoglobin 13.2, platelets 250, ESR 20, CRP 2.5.

Impression: bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw.

Plan:
1. Chlorhexidine 0.12% rinse twice daily.
2. Zoledronic acid discontinued - discussed with her oncologist, who agrees.
3. Avoid further dental extractions; gentle oral hygiene; acetaminophen for pain.
4. Return in about 3 months, sooner for drainage, fever or worsening swelling.

Otolaryngology

documents.title: Otolaryngology follow-up
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OTOLARYNGOLOGY
Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Date of service 12/18/2024

69-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer on letrozole who received zoledronic acid every 4 weeks for about a year until it was stopped in September, seen again for jaw pain. Pain has persisted for three months since the extraction about four months ago; she says the socket "never fully healed." No fever, trauma or recent infection.

Exam: exposed bone in the posterior mandible with surrounding gingival recession. No purulent drainage. No regional lymphadenopathy.

Panoramic radiograph today: sclerotic bone with areas of irregular lucency in the mandible at the extraction site.

Procedure: biopsy of the exposed lesion performed today under local anesthesia, sent to pathology.

Impression: persistent bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw; biopsy to exclude metastatic disease.

Plan: continue chlorhexidine rinse. We will call with pathology. Return in 3 months.

Otolaryngology

documents.title: Jaw biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ENT path in: necrotic bone with inflammatory debris, no malignancy. Called pt - she had already heard from ENT on 12/23 and was relieved. No change to plan.
